meta.title: SLATE grocery research, part three: the foods recipes ask for that a town had none of
meta.supplements: research-groceries.json and research-groceries2.json (same product schema). This file adds products only; it repeats no product already in those files.
meta.method: Read mechanically on 2026-10-04 from each chain's own catalogue feed, for each food a recipe asks for that the built catalog had none of in the chain's town, and for aubergine and canned pineapple, which no chain had: the Wynshop storefront search for Price Rite (store 301), The Fresh Grocer (197), Smart & Final (371) and SuperValu (5550); Giant Tiger's Shopify collections, the listing tagged for Ontario (mms_province_code:ON), a name listed twice for Ontario at two prices left out; Chedraui's VTEX catalogue search. Save-On-Foods' feed answered a Cloudflare challenge, and Tesco's and Sainsbury's refuse automated reads, so Vancouver's and London's gaps stand. A product's name must say the food and nothing it's made into, and it must come from the department that sells the food. Each at its regular shelf price: Giant Tiger's compare-at price or Chedraui's list price where higher; a Wynshop item on a temporary reduction is left out, its regular price not shown. The cheapest of each way a food is sold (by weight, by the pack, by the piece), two at most. A weighed item is priced by the pound or kilo, as the earlier files record one. sought is the food it was read for; brand is the feed's, where the name states it.
